newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares slip, market seen nervous. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares slip, market seen nervous. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]

text.p: Austrian shares continued to slip on Thursday, but managed recover from the day's lows, as investors nervously awaited the release of U.S. data for fresh clues on the direction of U.S. interest rates.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips fell 7.67 points, or 0.65 percent, to close at 1,168.89, up from an earlier low of 1,157.89. Among its constituents, 16 decliners outweighed five gainers.

But traders said the worst should be over now, saying the market was expected to bottom out in the near future. They noted strong technical support at 1,600 points in the ATX, with another support level at 1,500 points.
"Everybody is nervous ahead of the data," said one. "But as long as we manage to hold out at this level, everything's fine."

Steel maker VA Stahl lost 2.1 percent to close at 464.25 schillings after the group reported a 45 percent drop in net profits and said it would cut its 1996 dividend to 12 schillings from 13 schillings a year earlier.
"The result was within expectations, perhaps the only surprise was the cut in the dividend," a trader said.

Brewery group BBAG led the day's decliners, adding 4.17 percent to Wednesday's 3.1 percent fall to close at a new year-low of 690 schillings. The holding earlier this week rejected a takeover offer by drinks giant South African Breweries Inc.
On the positive side, BWT -- traded continously but not included in the ATX -- once again took the spotlight, adding another 8.73 percent to finish at a new year-high of 1,707 schillings.

The water-treatment company has seen its shares surge almost 37 percent over the past four weeks (corrects to four weeks from one week), as investors scrambled to buy the stock after the company announced last month it was developing a new technology that was expected to bring in substantial extra sales.
On the Vienna futures and options exchange, ATX futures for April delivery were down seven points at 1,163 on turnover of 1,598 contracts.
